technical_and_design_decisions: Use Spring Boot 3.x as the application foundation with embedded server on port 9393.
Use Spring Security as the unified security framework, with profile-based switching between file-based (U1) and LDAP (U2) authentication providers.
Implement role-based access control (U3) using Spring Security's HttpSecurity and method-level @PreAuthorize annotations with ADMIN and VIEWER authorities.
Implement the HDFS (U4), HBase (U6), and File Roll (U7) sinks as Spring Integration channel adapters following the existing source/sink pattern.
For U4 (Kerberized HDFS), use Hadoop's UserGroupInformation with Kerberos keytab and krb5.conf provided via externalized configuration.
For U6 (HBase), use the standard HBase Java client (ConnectionFactory) wrapped in a Spring Integration MessageHandler.
For U7 (File Roll), use Spring Integration's built-in FileRollingMessageHandler with size- and time-based rolling triggers.
For U8 (JMX source), use Spring Integration's JMX support (NotificationPublishingMessageHandler / NotificationListeningMessageSource) to publish notifications to a channel.
U5 is a spike/scoping activity per its acceptance criteria — deliverable is a design document only, no production code.
Use Maven multi-module structure if needed; single module assumed for this estimate.
Externalize all endpoint, security, sink, and source configuration in application.yml with profile-specific overrides.
assumptions: A working Spring Boot base project skeleton already exists (or can be created quickly); no greenfield project bootstrap from scratch.
Developer is experienced with Spring Boot, Spring Security, and Spring Integration.
Java 17+ toolchain is available and matches Spring Framework 6.x requirements.
Test infrastructure for HDFS (with Kerberos), HBase, LDAP, and JMX beans is available or can be stood up via Testcontainers / embedded servers.
Kerberos keytabs and krb5.conf files for U4 will be supplied by operations/QA; the developer only writes the integration code.
U1 and U2 are mutually exclusive authentication providers toggled via Spring profiles, not both active simultaneously.
U3 builds on top of whichever authentication mechanism (U1 or U2) is active, using role/authority mapping.
For U5, the spike covers research, design, and documentation only — implementation is out of scope for this increment.
Existing endpoint surface (the listed endpoints on port 9393) is already implemented; this increment only adds security and source/sink modules around it.
Unit tests, integration tests, and minimal user-facing documentation are included in each activity's effort.
No production deployment, performance tuning, or large-scale QA is included in this estimate.

activities.activity_description: Configure Spring Boot application, Maven build, dependencies (Spring Boot, Spring Security, Spring Integration, Hadoop, HBase client), externalized configuration structure, and base application bootstrapping on port 9393.

Set up the shared Spring Security configuration infrastructure: SecurityFilterChain, AuthenticationManager, password encoding, profile-driven provider selection, and base URL protection pattern applied to all listed endpoints.

Implement file-based user authentication using Spring Security's user-details-service backed by an externalized properties/YAML file. Include sample users with roles, password encoding, and integration tests.

Implement LDAP authentication using Spring Security's LdapAuthenticationProvider, configurable LDAP URL, user search base, user search filter, and group/authority mapping. Include integration tests using an embedded LDAP server (UnboundID/ApacheDS).

Define ADMIN and VIEWER roles, configure authorization rules in HttpSecurity (URL-level) and @PreAuthorize (method-level where applicable), map LDAP groups/file users to these roles, and add tests covering both roles.

Build a Spring Integration channel adapter sink that writes payload data to HDFS using the Hadoop FileSystem API, with Kerberos authentication via UserGroupInformation.loginUserFromKeytab. Externalize Kerberos principal, keytab path, krb5.conf path, NameNode URI, and target path. Include unit tests and an integration test using a Kerberized mini-HDFS cluster (e.g., MiniDFSCluster with Kerberos).

Research existing options for mass data ingestion from heterogeneous databases (Debezium, JDBC batching, database-specific CDC, Spring Cloud Stream + DB sources), collaborate with the team to determine the target design, and produce a written design specification document covering integration options, trade-offs, and recommendations. No production code is delivered.

Build a Spring Integration MessageHandler sink that writes payload data to HBase tables using the HBase Java client (Connection, Table, Put). Externalize ZooKeeper quorum, ZNode parent, table name, column family, and row-key strategy. Include unit tests and integration tests against an embedded or containerized HBase instance.

Build a Spring Integration FileRollingMessageHandler-based sink that writes events to the local file system with rolling triggered by file size and/or time. Externalize directory, file name pattern, max file size, and rotation interval. Include unit and integration tests.

Build a Spring Integration JMX source that subscribes to JMX notifications from one or more MBeans and publishes them as messages to a channel, using NotificationListeningMessageSource (or equivalent). Externalize MBean ObjectNames, notification filters, and output channel. Include unit and integration tests with a sample MBean.
Wire all modules together, run end-to-end test scenarios covering security (file and LDAP), role enforcement, and each sink/source module. Fix integration defects uncovered across module boundaries.
Produce README updates, per-module configuration reference, security setup guide (file-based and LDAP), and example properties snippets for HDFS (Kerberos), HBase, File Roll, and JMX source modules.
